newsitem.title: USA: CNA buys synthetic guaranteed investment business.
newsitem.headline: CNA buys synthetic guaranteed investment business.

text.p: CNA Financial Corp said Monday it acquired the synthetic guaranteed investment contract (GIC) business of Provident Life & Accident Insurance Co.
Provident Life is a unit of Provident Cos Inc.
This block of business has assets of more than $2.0 billion, CNA said.
CNA said the acquisition will give it an estimated five percent market share in the synthetic GIC arena, and will make it one of the three largest synthetic GIC writers in the insurance industry.

Synthetic GICs allow pension plans to retain ownership of the underlying assets while participating in asset performance, CNA said. For a fee, synthetic GIC writers guarantee the principal and book value for defined contribution plans.

CNA said its acquisition affects about 75 401(a) savings plans. Most of these plans represent employers with Fortune 500 standing. Although employers may choose to stay with Provident for the duration of the contract, CNA said it is "confident" that employers will switch to CNA.
"This acquisition demonstrates our commitment to the synthetic GIC business," Jeff Mohrenweiser, assistant vice president of pension markets at CNA, said in a statement.
CNA, which ranks among the top 10 U.S. insurance groups, had revenues in 1996 of $17.0 billion.
